title: Phase 1 complete: design settled
summary: Distilled two source systems into one generalizable .claude operating system after five analysis deep-dives and one adversarial review verified against real captured hook events.

title: Eight design decisions settled
summary: Sibling-folder RECORD_ROOT, allowlist redaction with raw kept forever, plain HTML console, commit-always push-ask, spines-only layers, one full profile with soft and hard evolution gears, stdlib core with uv as the extension tier, JSON handshake envelopes.

title: Thesis: three surfaces, one place each
summary: One place to interact (Claude Code), one place to control (the console), one command to evolve (/project-memory), on an always-on record behind fail-closed gates. Observability and governance are substrate, not surfaces.

title: Phase 2 foundation: _lib, configs, hooks, ritual runner
summary: Shared foundation with two-tier atomic writes and one journal vocabulary; five hooks split fail-closed (gates) from fail-open (telemetry); checkctl runs the ritual with a transaction checkpoint and a content-hash generator ledger.

title: Sub-agent bash denylist leaked to the main session
summary: policy.default.deny_bash applied to the orchestrator too, so the main session was denied git. Caught by the hooks smoke test before it ever ran live; the default block now applies to sub-agent identities only.

title: Phase 2 complete: the system runs on itself
summary: All 37 components built and probed, 140 tests green, and the full ritual (check, polish, publish) runs on this repo as one transaction. The record captured this session's own construction: 140k output tokens attributed across four models.

title: Opus adversarial code review found 3 critical and 7 important defects
summary: Review verified every finding empirically against the running system. Its central criticism was that docstrings asserted properties the code did not deliver, and that the 125 green tests confirmed the narrative rather than attacking it. All findings fixed, each with a regression test.

title: The policy gate could be switched off by writing a large file
summary: The hook passed the payload through an environment variable, which Linux caps at 128KB. A Write payload carries the file's whole content, so writing over ~128KB to a protected path made execve fail, python never ran, no decision was emitted, and the harness read silence as allow. Now the payload goes via a temp file and a non-zero judge exit fails closed.

title: Sealing silently destroyed distinct raw events
summary: Event identity was a second-precision timestamp plus fields hook events do not carry, so parallel sub-agents finishing in the same second collapsed into one row, discarding the rest from the tier documented as kept forever. A capture-time uniquifier now makes each event distinct.

title: The seal allowlist filtered key names but not values
summary: An allowlisted key holding a nested structure passed through verbatim, so a secret nested under an allowed field reached the redacted tier. Structured values are now replaced by shape markers; the verbatim original stays in out-of-repo raw.

title: Protected tree extended to every directory the gate executes from
summary: The gate imports _lib from .claude/tools on every tool call, but tools/, skills/ and console/ were unprotected, so a sub-agent could write the gate's own dependency and own it on the next call.

title: Human-agent bridge: required context/action + copy-context button
summary: need open now mechanically requires --context and --action written for a human reading cold; the console renders both per item with a copy button producing a paste-ready reply ending in 'My answer:'. Enforced in statectl, not by a sub-agent: the smallest primitive that guarantees the behavior.

title: Structured-output analysis engine
summary: obsctl analyze is now one OpenAI-compatible protocol (OpenRouter/Ollama/OpenAI/vLLM) with parallel chunked calls, json_schema structured output with fallback, repair, and mechanical taxonomy validation. Key from env only; labels fold into the story feed's analysis lane by plain code; the console gained its single POST action endpoint for it.

title: System map focus mode
summary: Click a component to fade everything unconnected and raise its neighborhood to the front; second click opens the detail popup; Esc clears. The connections are now traceable, which was the map's weakest point in first use.

title: Adoption smoke test: mechanics sound, nine frictions found
summary: A sub-agent adopted the system into a scratch repo by following /adopt literally: 37/37 probe, record isolated to the target's sibling, tests green. It also found two policy-gate bugs by dogfooding (git-path false positive, cross-project .claude-iff denial) and four skill gaps (CLAUDE.md instantiation unstated, unpassable placeholder grep, card-pruning wording that would delete core anatomy, mislabeled hooks-fire probe). All fixed with regression tests.

title: The governance held on real work
summary: The console sub-agent was denied writes to the protected .claude/console/ tree by the policy gate and returned its template as a proposal; the main session reviewed and applied it. The protected-tree mechanism proved itself unprompted on the first real multi-agent task after the hardening.

title: Distribution: two zips, a registered generator, and a release workflow
summary: distctl.py builds dot-claude-iff-fresh.zip and dot-claude-iff-adopt-kit.zip deterministically (fixed timestamps, write-gated) as a registered generator, so releases can never lag the repo. A GitHub Actions workflow tests then releases both on any v* tag.

title: README: stable work blocks + human collaboration guide + layout illustration
summary: Two sections teach the human half of the contract (brief like a colleague, answer via copy-context, debug with evidence, correct once then make it stick, close your blocks), with the side-by-side SVG showing the recommended layout across terminal, VS Code and desktop.

title: Billing mode: subscription is a truth, not an unknown
summary: model-prices.json gained billing api|subscription. Under subscription, dollar cost is not applicable: the empty-table warning goes quiet, the console reads 'in plan', and token counts keep flowing. Default set to subscription for this repo and the shipped zips.

title: Multi-page guided tour with progress tracking
summary: The docs tour is now ten pages (start, understand, setup, six exercises, finish) with shared tour.css/tour.js: a progress bar, per-page dots persisted in localStorage, prev/next and arrow-key navigation, all relative-linked so it works on Pages and over file://.

title: Demo console on the docs site
summary: docs/demo/console.html is the real console snapshotted from this repo by a new demo_build generator, flagged serverless so it badges 'demo snapshot' instead of polling. A visitor clicks the real 49-component map before installing anything.

title: README rebuilt around the six architecture decisions
summary: Verb-led front page: what it does in six verbs, then the decisions (context-carrying communication, managed memory, the progress pulse, one command to stop-publish-learn-evolve, the self-explaining map, merge-never-takeover adoption), a see-it table, star and issue links held to the system's own communication contract.

title: Showcase polish round: hero titles, one-line buttons, map legend, colored footer, motto pair
summary: Hero gained colored pane titles (console ocean, Claude Code orange) with matching dashes; three depth-styled buttons in one line with the Partner Guide banner beneath; the MAP tab opens with a kind-color legend; the console footer puts the timestamp and orange token total far left and the three colored links far right; both mottoes close the README and tour.

title: Edge colors are a disjoint family from node kinds
summary: Connections recolored to purples and pink (writes violet solid, reads light-purple dashed, invokes pink solid) so a line's hue can never be misread as a node's role; both legends now sit at the top of the MAP tab. The implemented relation taxonomy stays reads/writes/invokes from the card schema; feedback, human and validates remain reserved renderer styles to be promoted into card fields via evolution when real evidence needs them.

title: Showcase iteration round with the maintainer
summary: Live feedback loop over the public face: hero rebuilt with the triad annotations on top (control blue, remember green, interact orange) over the dashed side-by-side; responsive one-line blue buttons; dashed Partner Guide banner restored; keywords strip moved under the why paragraph; habits numbered in the guide and mirrored as a README dropdown with the maintainer's personal ADHD-household note.

title: Edge palette settled monochrome, superseding the purple family
summary: Connection colors went purple/pink first, then settled as black writes, dashed-black reads, gray invokes: node kinds keep the only hues on the map, edges read as pure structure. Relation taxonomy stays reads/writes/invokes; feedback, human and validates remain reserved styles pending evidence.

title: Tour top navigation and analysis card placement
summary: One row under the header divider: labeled Prev far left, centered clickable progress dots, labeled Next far right; the Retrospective analysis card moved to the end of STORY with a what-it-is and how-it-works info box, and its setup guide deduplicated.

title: v0.1.1 released
summary: Tag pushed, workflow green in 31 seconds, both zips attached and marked Latest. The release carries the tour, demo console, Partner Guide, analysis engine and the brand pass. An ultrareview of the branch delta returned zero findings.

title: Button wrap shipped: local screenshot check used a wider container than GitHub's
summary: The three README buttons at fixed 280px passed a 900px local render but wrapped to two lines on GitHub's real container; the maintainer caught it by screenshot. Fixed with percentage widths (31% each), which sidestep the container-width question entirely.

title: Evolution P1: theme-token-parity CHECK step
summary: First real retro proposal implemented: checkctl asserts the console template's two dark blocks define the identical custom-property set, turning the twice-in-one-day L-7 bug class into a ritual failure. Registered in phases.check with regression tests including a proof the shipped template passes its own gate.

title: Evolution P2: the width miss logged as lesson L-8
summary: Second retro proposal: the shipped visual defect became a lesson with a mechanical prevention (percentage widths for README assets; when fixed pixels are unavoidable, render local checks at or below 830px content width).

title: v0.2.0: the first post-evolution release
summary: Minor bump because the shipped system changed, not just its docs: the theme-parity ritual gate from the first real retro, the map's dual legends and monochrome edges, the console footer links and token total, the analysis info box, and the tour navigation. system_version now moves with the tag so adopters' drift warning keys correctly.

title: v0.2.1 - field-report hardening
summary: Fixed all confirmed findings from the first three real adoptions (issues #1-#3): Windows durable-write crash, distribution privacy leaks gated behind memory.json distribution.enabled with kits shipping it false and a git-tracked payload manifest, adopt-skill surgery (CLAUDE.md exclusion, history guard, sibling mode, decide-once console port), task-reality tokenizer, store.dist declaration, symbolic-ref removed from the read-only carve-out in both policy spots, gitignore-shadow lint, loud console port collisions.

title: Logo embedded across the three public surfaces
summary: The maintainer's spiral-of-people logo landed as docs/assets/logo.png with two derived assets: a one-row README footer pairing it with the joined motto, favicons plus topbar marks on all ten tour pages, and demo-only branding on the published console. The local console stays unbranded - the favicon and banner logo are injected behind the DATA.demo flag, so a machine's own console never gains web chrome.

title: The console build write-gate compared a subset of what it writes
summary: consolectl build compared payloads, not rendered pages, so a template edit with an unchanged payload never reached the output while the generator ledger marked it fresh; a wall-clock heartbeat age also made every build rewrite. Now it compares the full render, masking only generated_at and now.heartbeat_age_seconds.

title: Release changelog pinning, gated to the home repo
summary: CHANGELOG.md at the repo root (backfilled from every existing tag) plus a changelog_parity CHECK step that fails the ritual when a tag or the stamped system_version lacks its section, and a release recipe in the project-memory skill. Adopters never see any of it: the file sits outside the .claude/ tree the zips and the adopt skill copy, and the check rides the same distribution.enabled knob as the home-only generators.

title: The policy gate failed OPEN on Windows
summary: Four independent holes, all live in real sessions on this platform: the protected-tree ring built a backslash relative path and compared it to posix prefixes (so a sub-agent could write hooks, tools and configs); the record ring's mention regex could not capture drive-letter paths; the post-write validator exited before validating anything; and the PowerShell tool was absent from the PreToolUse matcher, leaving every ring open to one lane. Fixed with posix/normcase comparisons, case-folding where the filesystem is case-insensitive, and PowerShell judged like Bash.

title: Windows portability of the tools and the suite
summary: obsctl's transcript slug converted only '/' and '.', so ingest matched nothing on Windows and token tracking was silently empty; _lib.rel and _lib.tilde emitted backslash display paths that would have rewritten every card and console string on a Windows session. Both now normalize. The suite went from a fifth of it failing to fully green on this platform.

title: Console ports derive from the folder name
summary: The shipped default became "auto": each project derives a stable port from a hash of its folder name (7100-7899, walking forward on a collision) and the console answers on http://<folder>.localhost:<port>/ as well as the loopback IP. This retires the decide-a-port-per-project step and the everyone-collides-on-one-default problem; an explicit integer remains a decided-once override that still fails loudly. Rejected the alternative of one shared daemon serving every project by path: it needs global mutable state and puts all projects in one browser origin.

title: Optional system monitor and device identity
summary: sysmon.py probes CPU, RAM and NVIDIA GPU/VRAM with stdlib only, per-OS, failing open per metric; console.py serves it at /live/system.json behind an opt-in knob and the NOW tab renders a strip between needs-human and the journal. The samples are live-only by construction, so no committed surface or published demo can carry a machine's stats. Alongside it, state/machine.json records a salted user|host fingerprint and a human-chosen alias - never a username or hostname - and the session-start hook compares read-only, printing a loud DEVICE CHANGE line until statectl device names the box.

title: Stray runtime files written into the committed record surface
summary: A hand-rolled console launch used the wrong directory helper and dropped a pidfile and an empty log into .claude-iff/ instead of RECORD_ROOT. The gate correctly refused to delete them from the shell; they were removed with a disclosed script and journaled. The lesson is narrow: a manual launch of a service must mirror the hook's own paths rather than re-deriving them.

title: v0.2.2 - Windows gate hardening and a console that knows its machine
summary: Released with both distribution zips attached and the changelog section as its notes. Carries the Windows security fixes, the changelog machinery, derived console ports, the optional system monitor, device identity, and the logo. First release cut through the new recipe in the project-memory skill, and the first where changelog_parity gated the tag.
